analysis.title: Plenty Of Exposure, Zero Conviction: Goldman's Traders Dissect All The Latest Hedge Fund Positioning And Flows
key_insights: US fundamental L/S funds cut gross leverage by 8.7 points in a week to 207.5% (26th percentile one-year), the largest weekly drop since March 2020. Net leverage fell 3.7 points to 43.3%, the largest drop since the week of Liberation Day and the 0th percentile on a five-year lookback.

Across the global prime book, gross leverage rose 0.1 points to 314.2% (85th percentile one-year) while net fell to the 4th percentile and the L/S ratio to the 3rd. The note describes plenty of exposure with little conviction.
Global equities were net sold, with long sales outpacing short covers 5 to 1. Single stocks were net sold for an 8th straight week, while macro products were net bought for a 3rd straight week.

Hedge funds increased US-listed ETF shorts by 7% on Thursday Nov 5, the largest one-day increase since March, and 3.3% on the week, led by large cap equity ETFs. The note says a short base like this tends to fuel sharp bounces once selling exhausts.

Info Tech was by far the most net sold sector globally and in the US. Percentage selling in global tech was about on par with mid-October and September 2024, the largest net selling weeks on GS's record since 2016. Four of the top five global Info Tech selling weeks occurred in the past five months.

GS clients have net sold about $30B of tech (TMT + Comm Services) since the start of October, versus about $21-23B in July's momentum drawdown. Friday Nov 6 was the first buy skew in tech (+$1B) in 7 sessions.

US fundamental L/S funds lost 1.94% last week and global funds 1.48%, versus a 4.74% drop in the S&P total return index. US stock pickers are up 5.47% YTD against 8.43% for the S&P. Tech-focused funds erased their entire 2026 gain by Thursday.

Industrials were the second most net sold global sector, net sold for a 4th straight week with the largest percentage net selling in over 5 years. Electrical equipment and building products led, tied to the data center power trade after the midterm election.

Net allocation to Mag 7 and hyperscalers remains near record highs in the GS prime book. The book is net short housing and power/electrical equipment, and L/S ratios for homebuilders, restaurants and power are at 5-year lows.

CTAs sold an estimated $11.6B of S&P futures and $3B of Nasdaq futures over five days. Signals are negative in 50-60% of global equity markets. Baseline estimate is $23B of global equity futures sold over the next week and $45B over the next month, which would take the position to net short.

SPX CTA pivot levels are 7,675/7,676 (short term), 7,549 (medium term) and 7,084 (long term). Both short and medium levels are above Friday's close. In a flat tape CTAs sell about $31.1B of SPX in one week. They are sellers in every one-week scenario and turn buyers only in a strong one-month rally (about $14.4B into SPX).
US Panic Index hit 9.57 on Thursday and closed at 9.2. Readings above 9 have historically been a good buying opportunity.
SPX had the largest multiple surprise ratio in 19 years, with NDX in the top 2 and RTY in the top 5. Thursday was also the biggest put day in Cboe history.

Market plumbing was stressed: S&P futures top-of-book depth fell to $4.15MM against an $11.4MM average. One-month implied correlation rose toward 26% from about 10%. The Nasdaq vs S&P implied vol spread neared 9 points (record 12.6). Put skew is 1.20 and call skew 0.76.

GS risk appetite index is at -0.65, short of the -1 level Armbrust calls a strong buy signal (Covid low was -2.03). AAII bears rose to 48.4%, and CNN Fear & Greed is 24 (Extreme Fear). Retail buying was weakest since June.

Goldman's US Equity Sentiment Indicator rose to +0.6 from +0.2, far from the -1.0 light-positioning threshold. Non-dealers are net long $330B of US index futures (record $342B), and systematic strategies hold $181B of US equities.

Equity mutual funds took in $89B globally in the week to Nov 4 ($37B US), and $265B over 4 weeks, with technology funds again receiving the largest inflows. Asset managers' net long in S&P futures is 929K contracts versus a 767K 5-year average.

Corporate buybacks are accelerating as about 90% of the S&P is out of blackout. Discretionary open-market orders were 33% of desk flow versus 22% the prior week. 2026 YTD authorizations are $1.5T, above 2025's $1.37T. Issuance was $16.3B last week and $536B YTD.

Flood stays constructive: Q3 S&P EPS growth tracking 35% y/y (excluding mega-cap tech other income, median stock 14%), breadth improving from the narrowest since at least 2008, and the S&P at 18x P/E (31st percentile of the decade).

Investors are recalibrating data center build expectations after the midterm election (especially TX and OH). Market prices imply limited y/y capex growth in 2028, well below prior 30-40%+ expectations.
GS Research says semis are oversold and favors NVDA and AVGO (implying no growth from 2027), AMAT and LRCX in semi cap equipment. Memory is approaching oversold levels.

Week ahead: the S&P implied move through Friday is 2.29%. CPI is tomorrow (GIR expects +16bps core MoM). Last Friday's payrolls of +165k versus about 65k expected pushed December hike odds above 80%. Nvidia reports Nov 17.

The author leans against a durable bottom: CTAs, record-long index futures, hyperscaler longs, an unfinished risk-appetite gauge and a sentiment composite not at light positioning all point to more selling. The hedge fund capitulation may be done but the market bottom may be a few CTA programs away.

tension_points.bull_case: Gross and net leverage at multi-year lows leave less to sell. ETF shorts and a Panic Index above 9 point to a bounce. Flood cites 35% Q3 EPS growth, improving breadth, an 18x P/E and corporate buybacks. GS semis analysts call tech oversold.
tension_points.bear_case: CTAs are modeled to sell $31B of SPX in a flat tape, non-dealers hold near-record long index futures, hedge funds hold near-record hyperscaler longs, and risk appetite and sentiment composites are not at buy levels. Buybacks must absorb $536B of issuance.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Vol failing to stabilize, a hot CPI print tomorrow given December hike odds above 80%, or an Nvidia earnings disappointment on Nov 17. The medium-term pivot of 7,549 and the 7,675 short-term level remain above the market.
